title: Guided BatchSmith CLI and Quant Tutor
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds a guided CLI to generate tenant-level batching/caching defaults and an interactive 'quant tutor' to recommend quantization profiles. Includes telemetry hooks and docs; non-breaking.
commits: c1a2b3: add cli entrypoint and basic flow for guided batchsmith
d4e5f6: implement tenant sample analysis and heuristics engine
a7b8c9: add quant tutor REPL and profile suggestion service
f0e1d2: wire telemetry metrics + perf tests and smoke tests
9a8b7c: docs: CLI usage and troubleshooting guide
description:
Motivation: Customers increasingly ask for tenant-specific defaults that balance latency SLOs and unit economics without hand-tuning. This PR introduces two developer-facing tools: 1) a guided CLI (BatchSmith) that analyzes a tenant's request traces and proposes batching/caching presets (batch sizes, max wait, KV cache TTL suggestions, prefill hints); 2) an interactive 'Quant Tutor' assistant that runs a lightweight simulation over sampled requests and suggests quantization profiles (FP16/int8/4-bit mixes) with estimated token-cost and P50/P95 latency delta.

Summary of changes: Implemented a user-facing CLI binary (redwood-batchsmith) under cmd/ and a new internal package inference/econ/tutor that exposes the quant-suggestion API. Added a tenant sample analyzer that is conservative by default (prefers latency-safe presets) and a posterior score that estimates cost delta and quality risk. Instrumented telemetry: econ.batch.suggestion and econ.quant.tutor.* metrics, with tags for tenant_id/model/seq_dist. Included markdown docs and a quickstart in docs/cli/batchsmith.md.

Checklist: [x] tenant trace ingestion and sampling logic [x] heuristics engine + thresholds [x] quant simulation harness (fast, approximate) [x] telemetry metrics and dashboards links [x] unit + integration tests [x] docs and examples [x] canary rollout plan

Commits (high level): c1a2b3 entrypoint + command parsing; d4e5f6 sampling and heuristics; a7b8c9 quant tutor interactive flow; f0e1d2 perf harness and tests; 9a8b7c docs and examples.

Files changed (high level): cmd/batchsmith/main.go - new CLI entrypoint and flags; inference/econ/tenant_sampler.go - sampling and histogram helpers; inference/econ/heuristics.go - new rules and scoring; inference/econ/quant_tutor.go - quant simulation service; telemetry/metrics_registry.go - new metrics registered; docs/cli/batchsmith.md - usage and examples; scripts/canary_rollout.sh - deployment helper; tests/econ/* - unit and integration tests. Small illustrative snippet added to heuristics.go: if p95_latency > target && median_seq > prefill_threshold { suggest.prefill = true }

Review conversation excerpt: "Diego: Nice separation between sampling and scoring. Can you add an explicit lint check for max memory when simulating quant profiles?" "Asha: Added mem cap in a separate commit and updated tests to run the simulator with --max-mem flag." "Rina: Will the suggested presets be safe for low-traffic tenants? Add opt-out for automatic apply." "Asha: Defaults remain suggestions; CLI has --apply flag guarded by tenant admin scope. Documented in the quickstart." 

CI summary: unit tests 88 passed, integration smoke on staging passed, perf-run: simulated tenant sample (n=1000) shows median token-cost reduction of 9.4% and 95th latency increase of 1.9% on average for suggested quant profiles; end-to-end latency SLOs maintained for canary tenants. All checks green after two re-runs of the flaky e2e job.

Performance and safety notes: The quant simulator uses a sampled inference model and applies conservative error penalties; suggested profiles include an "estimated quality risk" tag (low/medium/high). For latency-sensitive tenants the default heuristic favors cache/prefill and FP16 over aggressive 4-bit quantization. We validated on three tenant canaries (tenant-a, tenant-b, tenant-c) with traffic shaping and rollback hooks. Cost win example: tenant-b sample estimated monthly token-cost savings of ~$18.2k on current usage with negligible change in observed quality metrics.

Canary and rollout: rolled to 5% of eligible tenants for 48h, monitored econ.batch.suggestion.accept_rate and customer reports. No regressions; proceeded to 25% on day 4. Merge includes a canary config and a safe rollback script (scripts/canary_rollout.sh). Operators should use the console dashboard link (dashboards/econ/batchsmith-suggestions) to monitor.

Backward compatibility: No API surface changes to existing inference endpoints. The CLI is additive. The quant tutor service is internal and behind a feature flag (econ.quant.tutor.enabled).

Follow-ups: automation to apply suggested presets as part of tenant onboarding (ENG-3590), and a telemetry privacy review for sampling windows (ENG-3421).
notes: Operator notes: feature flag econ.quant.tutor.enabled=false by default; CLI usage requires tenant-admin role or --apply explicit flag. See docs/cli/batchsmith.md for examples.
rollback_plan: scripts/canary_rollout.sh rollback <canary-id> will revert applied presets and stop traffic; telemetry alarms added to econ.batch.suggestion.error_rate and econ.quant.tutor.failures to auto-alert SRE.
